title: Hybrid argument for HMAC-DRBG non-adaptive PRG via the adjacent-hybrids invariant
intent: Close the final theorem of the HMAC-DRBG non-adaptive PRG proof -- the game distance | Pr[G_real] - Pr[G_ideal] | is at most numCalls times a per-step bound -- by three game-equivalence rewrites that put the distance into hybrid form (G_real == Gi_prg 0 == ... == Gi_prg numCalls == G_ideal), then one instantiation of the generic hybrid argument distance_le_prod_f on the single invariant Gi_adjacent_hybrids_close.

children.name: Gi_adjacent_hybrids_close
children.statement:
forall (n : nat),
  | Pr[Gi_prg n] - Pr[Gi_prg (S n)] | <= Gi_Gi_plus_1_bound.
children.closed_by: case split n <= numCalls \/ n > numCalls by lia; the in-bounds branch applies ratDistance_le_trans with Gi_prog_equiv_prf_oracle, Gi_replace_prf_with_rf_oracle, Gi_replace_rf_with_rb_oracle; the out-of-bounds branch rewrites Gi_adjacent_hybrids_close_outofbounds and closes by rat0_le_all; auto
children.note: The declaration header (`Theorem Gi_adjacent_hybrids_close :`, line 4519) carries an author comment on line 4520 between the `:` and the `forall`; the statement records the proposition alone, without that comment.

applicability.goal_shape: An inequality | Pr[G_real] - Pr[G_ideal] | <= numCalls * B between two probabilistic games G_real and G_ideal that differ by a parameter (how many PRF calls are replaced by random bits), where the parameter can be stepped one unit at a time through a family of intermediate games Gi_prg i with the same bound B per step.
applicability.use_when: the two games are linked by a family Gi_prg 0 ... Gi_prg numCalls with G_real == Gi_prg 0 and G_ideal == Gi_prg numCalls (so the endpoint rewrites are genuine ==, not just <=), a uniform per-step bound Gi_adjacent_hybrids_close holds for every adjacent pair, and a generic hybrid lemma (distance_le_prod_f here) is available to telescope the per-step bounds.
applicability.avoid_when: the adjacent-hybrids bound is not uniform in the index (it is the whole difficulty and must be a single statement); the endpoints only give one-sided inequalities so the three rewrites cannot turn the distance into hybrid form; or a hybrid step needs an adversary that does not factor into one uniform invariant.

consequences: The move concentrates all the difficulty into one invariant, Gi_adjacent_hybrids_close, which must bound every adjacent pair uniformly; the glue is then a wrapper (three rewrites plus one specialize of distance_le_prod_f). The three endpoint lemmas (Generate_move_v_update, G_real_is_first_hybrid, G_ideal_is_last_hybrid) must each be a genuine == so that rewrite applies; if an endpoint only gives a one-sided bound, the telescope does not go through. Failure modes: the per-step bound must be uniform in i (a fixed Gi_Gi_plus_1_bound independent of i); a non-uniform or endpoint-dependent bound forces the proof back into an explicit induction over i, and the single specialize step breaks.
